description: String length, bytes and case. MoonSharp strings are UTF-16 .NET strings: # counts code units and string.byte maps code units above 255 to 63 ('?').

cases.name: string.byte: Latin-1 range and above
cases.source: return { string.byte('A'), string.byte('é'), string.byte('ğ'), string.unicode('ğ'), string.byte('abc', 10) == nil }

cases.name: string.sub with negative and out-of-range indices
string.sub can split a surrogate pair
cases.source: local s = 'a👋b' return { s:sub(2, 3) == '👋', #s:sub(2, 2), string.unicode(s, 2), string.unicode(s, 3) }

cases.name: a lone surrogate cannot leave the host

expectError.messageContains: $: a string with an unpaired surrogate at code unit 1 has no JSON representation

cases.note: every transport would deliver it differently, so the host rejects it

cases.name: upper and lower are culture-invariant
cases.note: Lua 5.2 in the C locale changes only ASCII letters

cases.name: reverse swaps the halves of a surrogate pair
cases.source: local r = ('a👋'):reverse() return { #r, string.unicode(r, 1), string.unicode(r, 2), string.unicode(r, 3) }

cases.name: string.format %s pads and accepts numbers
cases.source: return { string.format('%s|%5s|%-5s|', 'x', 'ab', 'cd'), string.format('%s', 1.5), string.format('%10.4s|', 'abcdef'), string.format('%%'), string.format('%c%c', 72, 105) }

expectError.messageContains: strings.lua:(1,0-31): bad argument #2 to 'format' (string expected, got nil)

cases.name: comparison is by code unit
cases.note: Lua 5.2 compares with strcoll; in the C locale 'é' > 'z' as well

cases.name: tostring and type names
cases.source: return { tostring(nil), tostring(true), tostring(false), type(print), type(nil), type({}), type(''), type(2), type(coroutine.create(function() end)) }

cases.name: escapes in literals
cases.note: Lua 5.2 has no \u{} escape and reads it as an error
